items.name: Morgan Park Missing Middle mass rezoning (RS-3 -> RT-4, A-8970) — Superior Source site, 1320-38 W 109th Pl & 1425-29 W 109th (18 units)
items.attribution_rationale: Same enabling change as the Famor item: Mosley's aldermanic application A-8970 (O2025-0016179, sole primary sponsor, passed 2025-05-21) rezoned these Morgan Park blocks RS-3 -> RT-4 to facilitate Missing Middle construction. Superior Source Capital LLC's six three-flats ('six three-flat buildings housing 18 new units in Morgan Park' per mayor's Jan 21, 2026 release; 'six three-flats housing 18 new units' per Block Club) are on 1320-38 W 109th Pl and 1425-29 W 109th, inside the rezoned area; the three-flats require the RT-4 zoning Mosley introduced. The land-sale ordinance itself (O2025-0021689) was mayoral, so units are attributed to the alder-initiated rezoning.
items.notes: 1320-38 W 109th Pl is explicitly within A-8970's listed range (1233-1435 W 109th Pl). The second address is given as '1425-29 W. 109th St.' in the mayoral release (A-8970 lists 1201-1421 W 109th St, so 1425-29 would be just past the listed range) but as '1425-29 W. 109th Place' in Block Club, which is within the listed range.

_verify.reason: All four citations load. The 18-unit count is stated verbatim in the mayor's Jan 21 2026 release ('six three-flat buildings housing 18 new units in Morgan Park') and Block Club ('six three-flats housing 18 new units'). Kind=upzone is correct: RS-3 permits only detached houses; RT-4 (Residential Two-Flat, Townhouse and Multi-Unit) is what makes the three-flats legal. Attribution verified via eLMS API (matter E6E938F6-060C-F011-BAE3-001DD805116A): O2025-0016179 / App A-8970 has exactly one sponsor, Mosley, Ronnie L., filing office Ward 21, and the ordinance text bears his signature — he introduced it. Dates verified against eLMS: introduced 2025-04-16 (= first_public_date), passed 2025-05-21 (= date), both >= 2023-05-15; record number matches the required format. The St-vs-Pl ambiguity flagged in the item's notes is resolved in the item's favor: land-sale ordinance O2025-0021689 lists the six lots as 1429, 1427, 1425, 1338, 1322 and 1320 W 109th PLACE (the mayor's release's '1425-29 W. 109th St.' was its error; Block Club had it right), and an independent spot-check of the City zoning dataset shows every checked lot (1320, 1338, 1425, 1429 W 109th Pl) sits in an RT-4 polygon whose ordinance field is A8970 dated 2025-05-21 — all six lots were rezoned by Mosley's ordinance. 6 three-flats x 3 units = 18, consistent.

items.name: Morgan Park Missing Middle mass rezoning (RS-3 -> RT-4, A-8970) — Vazquez site, 1111-1240 W 110th Pl (15 units)
items.attribution_rationale: Mosley is the sole sponsor of aldermanic zoning application A-8970 (O2025-0016179; filing office Ward 21; ordinance text signed 'Ronnie L. Mosley, Alderman, 21st Ward'; introduced 2025-04-16, passed 2025-05-21 per the City Clerk eLMS API), which rezoned these Morgan Park blocks RS-3 -> RT-4 to facilitate Missing Middle construction — RS-3 permits only detached houses, so the RT-4 he introduced is what makes Vazquez Housing Development's five three-flats ('15 units are set for development' per the mayor's Jan 21, 2026 release; 'five three-flats with 15 units in all' per Block Club) legal. All five lots per land-sale ordinance O2025-0021688 (1235, 1240, 1222, 1200, 1111 W 110th Pl) are confirmed inside the A-8970 rezoning: the City of Chicago zoning dataset (dj47-wfun) shows each lot in an RT-4 polygon with ordinance A8970 dated 2025-05-21. The land-sale ordinance itself was a mayoral introduction, so units are attributed to the alder-initiated enabling rezoning.
items.notes: Address correction vs. the press-release wording: the mayor's release and Block Club describe the site as '1158-1240 W. 110th Place and 1235 W. 110th St.', but land-sale ordinance O2025-0021688's title lists the actual lots as 1235, 1240, 1222, 1200, and 1111 W 110th Pl (no 1158 lot; 1235 is on 110th Pl, not 110th St). All five fall within A-8970's listed common-address ranges (1101-1437 and 1200-1436 W 110th Pl) and were spot-verified as rezoned by A8970 on 2025-05-21 in the City zoning dataset. Developer history: site originally assigned to Toro Construction Corp. in the Aug 2025 selection; approved developer in Jan 2026 is Vazquez Housing Development; both iterations stated 15 units.

_verify.reason: Substantively sound but the site addresses (taken from the mayor's press release) are wrong. All citations load; 15 units is stated verbatim in the mayor's release ('15 units are set for development') and Block Club ('five three-flats with 15 units in all'). Mosley attribution, dates, and eLMS number verified as for item 1. However, land-sale ordinance O2025-0021688's title lists the five lots as 1235, 1240, 1222, 1200, and 1111 W 110th Pl — there is no 1158 lot, 1111 W 110th Pl is omitted from the item name, and '1235 W 110th St' is actually 1235 W 110th Pl. The rationale's claim that the range fits inside A-8970 survives anyway: City zoning dataset spot-checks show all five actual lots (1111, 1200, 1222, 1240, 1235 W 110th Pl) in RT-4 polygons with ordinance field A8970 dated 2025-05-21, i.e. every Vazquez lot was rezoned by Mosley's ordinance (1111 falls in the listed 1101-1437 W 110th Pl range). Corrected item fixes the name and notes to the ordinance's addresses; kind, units_delta, dates, eLMS number and citations unchanged.

rejected.item: Morgan Park Missing Middle mass rezoning (RS-3 -> RT-4, A-8970) — Famor site, W 109th Pl / 110th / 111th St (24 units)
rejected.reason: All four citations load and the 24-unit count is stated verbatim in the mayor's Jan 21 2026 release ('introduce 24 units to Morgan Park') and Block Club ('six four-flat buildings with 24 units in all'). Mosley attribution for A-8970 itself is solid (eLMS O2025-0016179: sole sponsor Mosley, filing office Ward 21, passed 2025-05-21). But the item fails the enablement check: the Famor land-sale ordinance O2025-0020977 identifies the six lots as 1409, 1335, 1333 W 109th Pl, 1435 W 110th Pl, and 1454, 1456 W 111th St. The legal text of A-8970 (attachment 'Morgan Park - Middle Missing - 21st Ward.pdf') bounds the rezoning at W 110th Pl / the alley next south of W 110th Pl — it never reaches W 111th St, and no W 111th St address appears in its common-address list. The City's zoning dataset (dj47-wfun) confirms the 111th St lots sit in an RT-4 polygon created by ordinance A4984 dated 2002-11-06, i.e. they were already RT-4 two decades before Mosley took office, while the other four lots show ordinance A8970 dated 2025-05-21. A Councilmatic search of all Mosley zoning ordinances touching W 111th St (A-9033, A-9038, O2025-0018192, etc.) found none covering 1454-1456 W 111th St. So Mosley's upzone enabled at most 4 of the 6 four-flats = 16 units, not 24. No citation states 16 (or any before/after pair yielding it), so under the registry rule that units_delta must appear verbatim in a citation, the item cannot be corrected — only re-added later at 16 units if a source directly stating a per-site split is found.

rejected.item: 10726-10750 S Loomis St rezoning for Missing Middle 'Cluster G' (A-9041) — Far South CDC three-flats (12 units)
rejected.reason: The eLMS record itself verifies cleanly: the City Clerk eLMS API confirms O2025-0018787 ('Zoning Reclassification Map No. 26-G at 10726-10750 S Loomis St - App No. A-9041'), filing sponsor Mosley, Ronnie L. (Ward 21), introduced 2025-07-16, passed 2025-09-25, and the ordinance PDF attachment is signed by Mosley and rezones M1-1/RS-3 to RT-4 (a real Mosley-initiated upzone). The DPD release states '12 planned units' and Urbanize states 12 total units (three condos per building) across 10726/10730/10734 S Loomis and 10717 S Glenroy. However, units_delta=12 is wrong for THIS ordinance: Chicago's current zoning dataset (data.cityofchicago.org dj47-wfun) shows the Loomis parcels are RT-4 via ordinance A-9041 (edit 2025-10-14), while the 10717 S Glenroy parcel is RT-4 under a separate case (23993) on a polygon created in the 2009 baseline remap — the fourth building's lot was never part of A-9041 and did not need it, so A-9041 enabled at most 3 of the 4 three-flats = 9 units. No citation states a 9-unit figure (9 only follows by multiplying 'three condos per building' by the subset of lots inside the rezoning, which fails the verbatim-count rule for upzones), so no compliant corrected_item exists: 12 is misattributed and 9 is uncitable. Additional defect: the councilmatic citation URL serves a different ordinance entirely (O2025-0016179, App No. A-8970, W 108th-110th streets, passed 2025-05-21) and does not document O2025-0018787. Block Club could not be fetched (HTTP 429) and chicago.gov returns 403 to automated fetch (content confirmed via browser-UA fetch). The item could be resubmitted at 9 units only if a source directly stating a 9-unit (three-building) count for the rezoned Loomis lots is found.

rejected.item: Garfield Green / Fifth City Commons upzone (C1-3 -> Planned Development, 201 S Kedzie Ave at Fifth Ave)
rejected.reason: Citations and mechanics check out: Chicago YIMBY (chicagoyimby.com/2022/01/zoning-approved-for-garfield-green-development-in-east-garfield-park.html) states the Council-approved rezoning from C1-3 to Planned Development allows 'up to 81 affordable residential units' (matches units_delta=81); the eLMS record confirms SO2021-1502 introduced 2021-04-21 and passed City Council 2021-12-15 (matches date and first_public_date); a Sun-Times spot-check also reports 81 units. However, attribution fails the initiation test. The eLMS record lists the sponsor as 'Misc. Transmittal' (applicant/DPD-filed), not Ervin. GPCC coverage says only that Ervin 'supported the project from the beginning' and praised POAH's community engagement; POAH's opening announcement contains a supportive quote. No source states Ervin introduced the ordinance, demanded the rezoning, or forced any change — this was a POAH-initiated development selected through the C40 Reinventing Cities program on city land. Support/championing of a developer-initiated, city-program project is explicitly insufficient under the initiation criterion, and the researcher's own rationale concedes the ordinance was 'applicant-filed by developer POAH via DPD transmittal, not introduced by Ervin.' Attribution is not a fixable field, so no correction is possible.

rejected.item: Hub32 upzone + city land sale (C1-5 -> B3-3, 132-136 N Kedzie Ave at Lake St)
rejected.reason: Citations and mechanics check out: Urbanize (chicago.urbanize.city/post/city-council-approves-revised-hub32-development) states the Council-approved rezoning C1-5 to B3-3 for a five-story, 51-unit all-affordable building scaled back from 63 units (matches units_delta=51); Chicago YIMBY corroborates 51 units; the eLMS record confirms O2025-0020567 (App No. 22908T1) passed City Council 2025-11-14 (matches date); Block Club spot-check also reports 51 units; first_public_date 2023-03-29 precedes date. However, attribution fails the initiation test. The eLMS sponsor is 'Misc. Transmittal' (applicant-filed), and the Council passage was moved by Alderperson Lawson, not Ervin. Hub 32 was selected by Mayor Lightfoot's administration through the Invest South/West East Garfield Park RFQ — a mayoral/city-wide program — and Ervin's only documented role is a supportive quote ('Hub 32 will improve a transit-oriented site...'). Neither Urbanize nor YIMBY coverage of the Council approval mentions Ervin at all. No source states he introduced the ordinance, demanded the rezoning, or forced the 63-to-51 reduction (the item's own notes attribute the reduction to costs). Support for a mayoral-program, developer-initiated project is explicitly insufficient under the initiation criterion; the researcher's rationale concedes the ordinance was 'applicant-filed via DPD transmittal, not introduced by Ervin.' Attribution is not a fixable field, so no correction is possible.
